# Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO

# Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] RRF is a useful baseline, but quality gains require evaluation. Bruch, Gai and Ingber found parameter sensitivity and a tuned convex score combination outperforming RRF in their tested settings. OpenSearch separately reports lower average NDCG@10 for RRF than its score-based hybrid baseline. Neither result establishes the best method for a specific MongoDB workload. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11934 · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/
- [statement] Native hybrid fusion is not unique to MongoDB: Redis describes single-query RRF and OpenSearch describes a server-side RRF search pipeline. A two-system architecture is therefore not the only alternative comparator. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-12) — https://redis.io/blog/reciprocal-rank-fusion/ · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/

## Structure and components

- [statement] Consolidation does not eliminate indexing or embedding costs: the MongoDB example generates embeddings and creates separate full-text and vector indexes. Any lower-TCO conclusion requires accounting for these retained components. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/harness-power-atlas-search-vector-search-with-rankfusion
- [statement] Atlas billing documentation lists hourly cluster charges and states that the cluster configuration estimate excludes data transfer. Comparing only that displayed estimate with another platform bill omits a documented cost component. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] In its published OpenSearch benchmark across six datasets, the project reports RRF averaging 3.86% lower NDCG@10, with mean latency improvements of 1.62% at p50 and 0.78% at p99 relative to score-based hybrid search. This compares fusion methods inside OpenSearch, not MongoDB against an external vector database. (low confidence) — https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/
- [statement] The OpenSearch benchmark prose says RRF consistently improves latency, but its table includes regressions: Quora p50 rises from 167 to 170 ms and SciDocs p99 from 156.02 to 159.015 ms. Aggregate improvements can conceal workload regressions. (low confidence) — https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB supports combining $search and $vectorSearch with $rankFusion in one query. RRF uses rank positions rather than raw lexical/vector scores, avoiding the need to normalize incompatible score scales. This reduces fusion integration work but does not eliminate either retrieval operation. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://redis.io/blog/reciprocal-rank-fusion/
- [statement] The MongoDB hybrid-search documentation snapshot states that fusion input pipelines must query the same collection, run serially rather than in parallel, and do not support pagination. These are deployment and latency constraints to check before replacing a two-system implementation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md
- [statement] Inference for a latency comparison: native fusion is not guaranteed to beat parallel application queries. MongoDB documents serial sub-pipelines; Redis explains that parallel retrieval tracks the slower retriever rather than the sum, and that candidate retrieval usually costs more than RRF arithmetic. Network, queueing and fusion overhead still need measurement. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://redis.io/blog/reciprocal-rank-fusion/
- [statement] One synthetic-marketplace repository reports a 2026-10-06 run with native $rankFusion p50/p95 of 502/3175 ms versus 402/475 ms for parallel queries plus application RRF. The author explicitly limits the measurements to that cluster and run. Both paths use Atlas; this is not a two-vendor TCO benchmark or a controlled proof of general latency differences. (low confidence) — https://github.com/adrianofratelli-glitch/atlas-search-vs-vector-marketplace
- [statement] Inference for TCO evaluation: compare infrastructure and data-transfer charges together with measured client-fusion and synchronization maintenance, rather than pricing only the RRF calculation. Atlas billing describes hourly cluster charges and data-transfer costs; the marketplace implementation demonstrates that synchronization work can remain within a consolidated deployment. No universal savings percentage follows from these sources. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://github.com/adrianofratelli-glitch/atlas-search-vs-vector-marketplace, https://redis.io/blog/reciprocal-rank-fusion/
- [statement] RRF combines rank positions rather than raw relevance scores, avoiding direct addition of incompatible BM25 and vector score scales. This simplifies fusion but does not remove retrieval work. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://redis.io/blog/reciprocal-rank-fusion/, https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] That repository keeps a catalog and vector copy in separate collections, maintains a change-stream mirror in application code, and adds a lexical index on the vector collection to meet native fusion requirements. Inference: platform consolidation alone does not guarantee that a particular data layout eliminates synchronization code or duplicated storage. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/adrianofratelli-glitch/atlas-search-vs-vector-marketplace · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md
- [statement] MongoDB can combine full-text and vector retrieval with $rankFusion in one query; its implementation example removes client-side result-merging logic while retaining both search paths. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/harness-power-atlas-search-vector-search-with-rankfusion
- [statement] MongoDB documents that fusion sub-pipelines execute serially and target one collection. Redis recommends parallel retrieval so latency tracks the slower path. Inference: native MongoDB fusion must be benchmarked against parallel client orchestration before claiming a latency advantage. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/hybrid-search/hybrid-search-overview.md · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://redis.io/blog/reciprocal-rank-fusion/
- [statement] MongoDB's native-fusion example removes client-side result merging but still requires an Atlas cluster with Search, an embedding service, and indexed text fields and vector embeddings. Pureinsights identifies external-search synchronization troubleshooting, developer efficiency, and DevOps deployment, monitoring and management as operational concerns. These architecture descriptions do not report a controlled total-cost comparison at matched search quality and throughput. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/harness-power-atlas-search-vector-search-with-rankfusion · keywords: Hybrid search ($rankFusion) vs two-system fusion TCO · also: https://redis.io/blog/reciprocal-rank-fusion/, https://opensearch.org/blog/introducing-reciprocal-rank-fusion-hybrid-search/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing.md, https://pureinsights.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Solution-Brief-Atlas-Search-Migration-Services-V4.pdf
